## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 11, titled *Bhedānuvattaka* ("Siding with a schismatic"), is the eleventh training rule in the *saṅghādisesa* (formal suspension) chapter of the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The rule addresses monks who associate with and support a fellow monk attempting to instigate a schism (*saṅghabheda*) in the monastic community; persisting in such factional support despite formal admonition incurs the severe ecclesiastical penalty of suspension [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. None of the sampled references in the secondary literature corpus directly discuss this rule, as keyword matches for "ss 11" in the dossier represent unrelated section markers in philosophical or narrative treatises.
According to SuttaCentral, full parallels to this rule exist across virtually all surviving monastic lineages [SuttaCentral]. Curated parallels include the corresponding Bhikkhu Pātimokkha rule (*pli-tv-bu-pm-ss11*), the Parivāra, the Bhikkhunī Vinaya (*pli-tv-bi-vb-ss15*), and the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga traditions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, Lokottaravāda, and Dharmaguptaka preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan, as well as the Upāliparipṛcchā [SuttaCentral].
